To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mushroom bodies of adult crickets contain a population of Kenyon cells that sprout processes in the perikarya and in fiber bundles.
the mushroom body neuropil is a site for the growth and maturation of Kenyon cell fibers, and that the perikaryonal layer of the mushroom body is a site for neurogenesis in adult crickets.
the Kenyon cells are a heterogeneous population of neurons with a variety of morphologies.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the form, distribution and cytology of mushroom bodies (MB) in adult cricket brains, and in particular, with the growth of Kenyon cells (KCs), a subset of local interneurons that are involved in olfaction and gustation, learning, memory, and motor control.
the form and function of mushroom body neuropil, and with the generation of new neurons in adult cricket brains
the growth of mushroom bodies in adult cricket brains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mushroom body is not a static, but rather a dynamic structure.
in crickets the mushroom body neuropils are formed by a combination of growth of existing Kenyon cell fibers and the generation of additional Kenyon cells.
the Kenyon cell system in crickets is a dynamic structure, which continues to grow throughout adult life.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified and described a novel population of mushroom body interneurons in adult insects, the sprouting Kenyon cells.
we describe a subset of mushroom body Kenyon cells in a cricket brain that are still growing in adulthood.

the Kenyon cell population in the mushroom bodies of adult crickets contains a significant number of neurons that continue to grow and mature throughout life, and that these neurons are not simply a subset of the Kenyon cells that were born during the last larval molt.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Kenyon cells are not born as adult‐like neurons but are generated as stem cells that differentiate into neurons.
the adult cricket brain has the potential to generate new Kenyon cells and that these neurons have a unique morphology.
the mushroom body of adult cricket brains is a dynamic structure.
